# PREREG_N -- pass 8, campaign N (cluster grain)

**Frozen 2026-07-27, while campaign N has ZERO runs.** Base commit 2da19be. Do not edit this file
after the first run dir under `if_repair/runs/campaigns/N/` exists.

## What motivated this campaign (and why that does not contaminate it)

`p8_cluster_grain.py` scored every frozen config in `p7_pooled_oos.CONFIGS` against Stage F's 72
cluster masks -- a draw built as attribution-agnostic ground truth in the original project and,
per pass 7's HANDOFF open thread #3, never used for attribution. Conditional on target-in-mask
(n=40), primary outcome `plain`, Kendall tau_b:

| config | target | rho | GradDot_dmean | delta | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| relatif_C5 | C5 | -0.224 | **+0.239** | -0.463 | [-0.728, -0.219] |
| surrogate_C5 | C5 | -0.079 | +0.198 | -0.277 | [-0.582, +0.035] |
| ensemble_C5 | C5 | -0.239 | +0.239 | -0.479 | [-0.745, -0.230] |
| leverage_C7 | C7 | -0.198 | **+0.427** | -0.625 | [-0.834, -0.430] |

Two things in that table, neither of which this campaign is allowed to assume:

1. **The plain GradDot baseline is strongly positive at cluster grain** (+0.239 on C5, +0.427 on
   C7 Kendall; +0.347 / +0.605 Spearman) on a draw it was never tuned against. Nothing at demo
   grain in seven passes reached this.
2. **Every self-influence / leverage correction reverses sign.** The corrections that were the
   whole subject of passes 4-7 are actively harmful at cluster grain.

That table is a SCAN over one draw. It selects the hypothesis; it cannot also test it. Campaign N
is a fresh, disjoint draw, and this file is frozen before it runs.

## Hypothesis of record

**FAMILY OF ONE, so alpha = 0.05, one-sided.**

> **N1.** At cluster grain, on campaign N's fresh masks, `GradDot_dmean` (the frozen
> `p7_pooled_oos._graddot("cached")` config, imported not re-implemented) clears the **absolute
> half-ceiling bar** on target **C5**: conditional LDS rho >= 0.5 x cluster-grain noise ceiling,
> both computed within campaign N under the primary statistic.

Why the absolute bar and not a paired one: pass 7's HANDOFF open thread #4 asks whether the
half-ceiling bar is unreachable for every estimator anyone would try, in which case it measures
the ceiling rather than discriminating hypotheses. Seven passes failed it at demo grain. If a
plain, uncorrected estimator clears it as soon as the unit is 15 demos instead of 1, the bar was
fine and the grain was the problem. That is the pass's claim, so that is what gets tested.

Why **C5** when C7 looked stronger on Stage F (+0.427 vs +0.239): C5 is the target every pass-4/5/6
hypothesis was written about and the target of three of the four frozen configs. Choosing the
weaker of the two on the discovery scan is deliberate -- it makes the primary immune to the charge
that the target was picked for its Stage F magnitude. C7 is reported as secondary.

## Statistic (chosen blind, `p8_design.py --stage statistic`, committed before any contrast)

**Primary: Kendall tau_b.** **Mandatory secondary: Spearman**, for continuity with every
historical number in this repo. Both bars reported under both.

Selected on reliability and noise ONLY (BLOCKERS #30), by the resolution criterion pass 7 used:

| statistic | split-half r | Spearman-Brown | noise c (sd = c/sqrt n) | resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kendall tau_b | 0.437 | 0.579 | 0.543 | **10.68** |
| Spearman | 0.499 | 0.622 | 0.717 | 8.67 |

Spearman is the more reliable statistic at cluster grain and Kendall the less noisy one -- the two
criteria disagree here, unlike at demo grain. Resolution (reliability / noise) settles it at
1.23x for Kendall. The contrast was not computed under either statistic before this choice.

**The ceiling must be computed under the same statistic as the LDS it bounds.** `lds.noise_ceiling`
is a Spearman recipe; `confirm_nseries.py` uses the pluggable split-half construction from
`confirm_mseries.ceiling` so that the Kendall bar is a Kendall bar. Spearman-Brown is derived for
correlations, so the Kendall ceiling is an approximation and is labelled as such wherever reported.

## Design

**Masks: 278, complete enumeration of |S| in {4,5,6} minus Stage F's signatures**
(`p8_masks.py`, manifest committed with the campaign at zero runs).

| stratum | space | excluded | fresh | balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 of 9 | 126 | 0 | 126 | exact, 56/cluster |
| 5 of 9 | 126 | 58 | 68 | 36-40/cluster |
| 6 of 9 | 84 | 0 | 84 | exact, 56/cluster |

Enumeration replaces Stage F's randomized construction because the space is small enough to
exhaust; a complete stratum is exactly balanced with exactly uniform co-inclusion, and disjointness
from Stage F is exact set difference. **Stage F's 72 masks carry only 58 distinct signatures** --
its swap-repair construction repeated 14 subsets, which bought seed depth rather than coverage.
Every conditional-n reported against Stage F, including the table above, is optimistic by that
factor.

**|S| is a stratum, not a covariate to pool over.** It sets the training-set size (60/75/90 demos),
which moves the outcome directly. Reported per stratum and pooled with |S| controlled, mirroring
the in-target-count partial already in `src/analysis.demo_grain_lds`.

**Depth: 5 seeds, job list ordered SEED-MAJOR.** At cluster grain the mask axis is capped at 336
subsets total and campaign N consumes 278 of them, so depth is the only remaining axis -- the
inverse of BLOCKERS #29's demo-grain rule, and a consequence of the combinatorics rather than a
contradiction of it. Depth >= 4 also lets the noise ceiling be computed on all 278 masks instead
of Stage F's 12, which `p8_design --stage ceiling` showed is the weakest number in the comparison
(conditional CIs as wide as [-0.03, +0.81] on 6-8 masks). Seed-major ordering means the design is
balanced at every prefix of the job list.

Projected conditional paired sd at ~139 masks: **0.046** (Kendall), 0.061 (Spearman).

## Stopping rule (prespecified, outcome-blind)

Campaign N is time-boxed. **The analysis uses the largest depth d such that all 278 masks have d
completed seeds.** Because the job list is seed-major, that prefix is always a complete, balanced
design. The depth is read off the run directory, never off the outcomes. No optional stopping: the
result is computed once, at that depth, whatever it says.

## Scored exactly once

`confirm_nseries.py` refuses to overwrite an existing result file. p = 0.057 on campaign M is
exactly the situation `p7_prereg.md` §7 exists to protect; the same rule binds here.

## Secondary and descriptive (no alpha, no inferential claim)

- C7 and the remaining seven targets under both statistics.
- The four frozen corrections vs `GradDot_dmean` -- does the Stage F sign reversal replicate?
- Per-stratum breakdown; the |S| trend.
- Cluster-grain vs demo-grain side by side (the pass's teaching artifact).

## Known difference from the Stage F scan

Stage F outcomes come from the original project's probe battery (`src/evaluate.py`); campaign N
outcomes come from `if_repair.retrain.heldout_frame_losses`, the pipeline every campaign A-M and
every pass-7 number used. **The primary bar is computed entirely within campaign N** -- both the
LDS and the ceiling -- so the comparison is internally consistent. Agreement with the Stage F scan
across two different outcome pipelines would be a robustness result; disagreement would be a
finding about the pipelines, and either way it is reported, not reconciled after the fact.
